name: Can you build an ADU kitchen without a dishwasher hookup?

mainEntity.name: Is it acceptable to leave out the dishwasher plumbing and still have a complete ADU kitchen?
mainEntity.text: Is it acceptable to leave out the dishwasher plumbing and still have a complete ADU kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: A dishwasher hookup is not always necessary in an ADU kitchen, especially when space is tight or the unit is intended for light use. Removing the dishwasher can free up cabinet storage, widen circulation, and simplify plumbing and electrical work. That can be a smart choice in a very small ADU or a JADU-style layout where every inch matters. The downside is reduced convenience and possibly a less premium feel if the unit is being marketed for longer-term occupancy. Many homeowners compromise by planning the space so a dishwasher could be added later, even if it is not installed initially. That keeps the kitchen flexible without committing to the extra cost upfront. The best decision depends on how the ADU will be used, whether the sink and storage are robust enough to handle dishwashing manually, and how much room the layout can truly spare. A good design makes the omission feel intentional rather than like a missing feature.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, an ADU kitchen can still function without a dishwasher hookup if it has the required core kitchen components and enough sink and storage space. Leaving out the dishwasher can save space and reduce cost, especially in very small units. The tradeoff is lower convenience and possibly lower rental appeal.
